comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
Thanks, that detail cracked it — "unchecked but it still reconnects last sessions" pointed straight at a real bug. 🎯

There were **two** separate "reopen last session" mechanisms, and only one of them honored your **Reconnect on startup** checkbox. The other — the one that restores your saved window layout — was reopening every connection tab that was open when you last closed mRemoteNG, *regardless* of that setting. With your 132-connection SQL setup that's a lot of sessions firing at once, whi...

comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
Found it, @kaansengul — and your 54s number ended up matching the math exactly.

**Root cause:** after loading your connections from SQL Server (which itself is fast), mRemoteNG writes a local offline-fallback cache of the connection tree. That cache write re-encrypts every stored password with PBKDF2 at 600,000 iterations — and it was deriving a **fresh key for every single field**. 132 connections × ~0.4s per derivation on a typical laptop ≈ 54 seconds, all spent on the startup path. (The same...

comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
One more startup win landed on top of yesterday's fix: the schema check that runs before loading your connections was issuing ~200 sequential queries against the database on every startup — it's now a single query (`0ff3a8862`). If your SQL Server is remote, this shaves a few extra seconds on top of the PBKDF2 fix.

Grab tomorrow's nightly (or any build after this commit) for the retest — it includes both fixes, and the `[Startup] LoadConnections:` line should now be well under a second.
